reasons.title: Why We're Chosen
reasons.lead: By working together, our two companies provide consistent support from pre-hire consultation through retention after onboarding.

items.title: Matching grounded in care-field understanding
items.desc: From a care provider's perspective, we clarify the kind of person a facility needs and aim to propose candidates who fit the field.

items.title: An integrated system linking recruitment, education and acceptance support
items.desc: From overseas recruitment, selection and education to residence-status procedures and acceptance preparation, all linked within a single system.

items.title: Retention support that continues after onboarding
items.desc: We continue retention-focused support after onboarding, including regular interviews, Japanese-language study and follow-up on field challenges.

talent.title: The talent we introduce
talent.lead: We introduce candidates who meet the requirements for the Specified Skilled Worker «Care» field and have completed selection and prior education.
items: Talent who meet the requirements for the Specified Skilled Worker «Care» field
Japanese ability meeting requirements such as JLPT N4 or JFT-Basic
Passing required tests such as the Care Skills Evaluation Test
Confirmation of character and aptitude through interviews
Completion of pre-arrival Japanese and basic care education
talent.note: Each candidate's experience, aptitude and Japanese ability differ. We'll explain the details when we talk.

steps.text: Education in Japanese・Japanese culture・care fundamentals

items.q: How long does it take from consultation to onboarding?
items.a: From candidate selection through residence-status application and acquisition to entry procedures and onboarding, it generally takes several months. Since this varies by timing and conditions, we'll share an estimate when we talk.

items.q: What level of Japanese do candidates have?
items.a: We introduce candidates who meet the Specified Skilled Worker «Care» requirement of JLPT N4 equivalent or JFT-Basic. Japanese ability differs from person to person, so you can confirm it during the interview.

items.q: Do we need to prepare housing?
items.a: In principle the receiving facility arranges it, but we can support everything from finding a property to signing the contract and arranging household goods. Please consult us for details.

items.q: What support is there after onboarding?
items.a: We continue retention-focused support, including regular interviews, ongoing Japanese-language study, daily-life and work follow-up, and responding to challenges that arise on the floor.

items.q: What is included in the fees?
items.a: The introduction fee includes the residence-status application fee. The support fee is monthly. Some items, such as travel costs and housing support, are charged separately at cost. Please see the cost section for details.

items.q: Can facilities hiring foreign workers for the first time consult you?
items.a: Yes. We support you from the very first consultation, including building the system and acceptance framework. Please feel free to reach out.

education.title: What produces reliable talent is education
education.lead1: What the care floor needs is talent ready to contribute. And the single greatest factor in producing that talent is education.
education.lead2: To develop truly capable talent, both are essential — knowledge of the care floor, and knowledge of educating foreign nationals.
education.centerLabel: The overseas talent care staff want
education.history: Since 2019 we have jointly run a care-education center in Hanoi, Vietnam, with certified care-worker (kaigofukushishi) Japanese instructors delivering education at the industry's highest standard. That system continues today and is expanding to new countries.
education.highlight: With pre-arrival education plus three months after arrival, talent who can follow care staff's instructions

nepal.title: Why we recommend Nepal now
nepal.lead: The country that "fits" the care floor — that is Nepal. When it comes to care, the reasons to recommend Nepal are clear.

items.title: Many women aspire to care work
items.desc: Many women hope to work in care, giving a wide choice of candidates. It's easier to meet floors that want female staff.

items.title: They settle in and rarely leave
items.desc: Many prefer to work long-term in Japan rather than return home, so they stay stably and for the long run.

items.title: Japanese comes easily
items.desc: The talent market has many people studying Japanese, and the grammar is close to Japanese, so they pick it up quickly.

items.title: Character and culture suited to care
items.desc: A culture of caring for the elderly is deeply rooted; many are gentle and sincere, fitting in easily on the care floor.

privacy.lead: Momokichi Co., Ltd. × ITM Japan complies with the Act on the Protection of Personal Information (APPI) and handles personal data appropriately.

Except as required by law, we do not provide personal data to third parties without the person's consent.
We take appropriate security measures to prevent unauthorized access to and leakage of personal data.
Upon request, we respond to disclosure, correction, or deletion of retained personal data.
For inquiries about the handling of personal information, please contact us via the form.
